title: Bob Carroll and the rehearsal with Jesse Stone
summary: Bob Carroll was a comical, outspoken tenor who clashed with Jesse Stone at a rehearsal for the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: But you know there was another tenor that I always used to think was good, never got mentioned much -- Bob Carroll. Do you remember him?
Bob Carroll, him and I were very good buddies.

Now, he was a fine tenor player, but Bob -- I could do more with Bob, I guess, and Ben than anybody. They all liked me. They liked my style of playing. He had a peculiar way of playing, beautiful thing. He played, you know, interpretations. And one day we were rehearsing to go to the Apollo Theater. So they had (unintelligible) on bass. So Jesse Stone had did the arranging.
Jesse Jones -- Jesse Stone -- he the one that wrote 'Idaho'.

And he was very talented arranger, you know. So he would write parts like for the reeds, brass, like baritone, sax, bass and trombone, he would -- you know, he had that thing (unintelligible) with him. So we would

rehearse, were rehearsing. Bob was a character, really character, you know. We'd -- let the reed section run off our parts, and everything Jesse said (unintelligible) fine, and beautiful. So we'd lay the horns down. There's something wrong, some passages there, that bass and baritone sax and the trombones, he had a part played from the passages. So Bob was comical anyway, Bob. I said, what do you say, Bob? He said, huh, man, we've been here a whole three hours playing, practicing, rehearsing, and that cutback tone, that bass. I said, Bob, said, he'll get together later on. What? That (unintelligible) too, Bob. I said, let's go on out and get a little taste right around the Braddock there. We were rehearsing down in the Braddock Hotel.

So Bob started to talk, said, I'm going to straighten that son of a bitch out. I said, Bob, leave the man alone. Well, (unintelligible) came back, he said, fellows, we going to learn this (unintelligible) again. So Bob said, hey, Jesse, -- what do you want to do now? He said, same thing. Well, the saxophone section, we got ours, said, what's wrong with that passage (unintelligible), said, everybody playing it but the trombones and the baritone and the trombone, but the bass player ain't reading that. That started the argument.
So I'm trying to keep Bob quiet. That didn't do no good. I got to tell him, I said, Bob, don't pay no mind.

Why not tell him, man? I said, Bob, you going to start confusing (unintelligible). You don't start that foolishness. (UNintelligible). Hey, look, you take that part home and practice, because you ain't playing nothing on that music. Then Brand got mad. They broke up (unintelligible). Oh, Lord, they broke up the rehearsal. I walked, picked my knife out (unintelligible). Bob said, take the saxophone. I said, oh, boy.
But that's the way Bob was. Bob Carroll, Ben Webster and Bob Dorsey --
